## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Sekhiya 63 of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (*Yāna*, "Sitting in a vehicle") is a training rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates monastic decorum regarding teaching the Dhamma, specifically prohibiting monastics from reciting or expounding the teachings to someone who is seated in or riding a vehicle, provided the person is not ill [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels for this training rule are preserved widely across both male and female monastic codes in the Vinayas of multiple early Buddhist schools, including Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Lokottaravāda recensions extant in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan, alongside the Pali Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, and Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Computationally, DharmaNexus records 105 matching passages across 32 Pali texts, showing extensive formulaic text reuse with adjacent Sekhiya rules concerning inappropriate situations for teaching the Dhamma (notably Sekhiyas 58–72 and 74), as well as corresponding segments in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* and the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* commentary [DharmaNexus].
